title: openai: /v1/chat.completions parity - roles, stop/logprobs, streaming stability & structured output
author: Priya Natarajan
body: Motivation: Improve Redwood's OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat.completions endpoint parity to cover roles, stop tokens, logprobs, structured output formatting, and make streaming more robust for edge cases (partial chunks, function calls, and fast client disconnects). This PR unblocks customers relying on exact OpenAI semantics and fixes several compatibility regressions introduced during streaming refactors. What changed (summary): - Implemented role-preserving mapping for assistant/system/user messages and added explicit validation for role values to match OpenAI's expectations. - Added support for 'stop' sequences for chat completion requests; stop handling integrates with our streaming path and truncate logic. - Exposed per-token logprobs when requested (logprobs parameter) with consistent JSON formatting between streaming and non-streaming responses. - Stabilized streaming by reworking chunk flush boundaries, adding backpressure handling for slow clients, and fixing an off-by-one in sequence length accounting that caused truncated final tokens. - Introduced structured output helpers to honor content-type hints and function call formatting (name/arguments) in both streaming and final responses. - Added compatibility fallbacks for models that do not support logprobs or function-calling; behavior documented in the API compatibility notes. Key files changed and why: see files_changed list. Checklist: [x] Unit tests for role validation and stop sequence trimming. [x] Integration tests covering streaming + stop tokens + function call boundaries. [x] E2E smoke against GPT-compatible test harness. [x] Docs updates for compatibility notes and example payloads. [x] Perf check for streaming latency impact (<= 3% median increase under typical load). Testing notes: Ran our streaming perf canary (perf-canary) with 5k concurrent chat streams; median p99 latency increased by ~2.1% which is acceptable given correctness improvements. One flaky test in CI (streaming/chunking) failed on first run; rerun passed. Also validated responses against OpenAI-compat test vectors (see linked Linear items). Backward compatibility / migration: This change is additive from an API surface perspective. If a model backend does not support logprobs or function calling, we return compatibility fallback responses (nulls or best-effort fields) rather than errors. No breaking changes anticipated. References: ENG-4821, ENG-4892, PM-147. Full description and implementation details are in the commits below.
commits: a1: openai: implement role mapping and strict validation for chat messages
a2: openai: add stop sequence handling to tokenizer + streaming truncation
a3: openai: surface per-token logprobs in streaming and non-streaming responses
a4: streaming: fix chunk boundary off-by-one and add backpressure handling
a5: api: structured output helpers + function call formatting integration
a6: docs: update openai-compat notes and examples for chat.completions
review_comments: Evan Moore: Looks good overall - left a nit on the stop-sequence tests about edge-case empty tokens.
Sofia Alvarez: Please add a unit for logprobs when model returns sparse logits (we saw nulls in older models).
Kenji Yamamoto: Confirmed the backpressure approach is safe for dedicated pools; recommended a small comment in backpressure.py.
Aisha Rahman: Docs example for function-calls is helpful, but show explicit example of name-only vs name+arguments.
Priya Natarajan (author): Addressed comments; added test for sparse-logits and clarified examples in docs. Reran canary and CI.
SRE Bot: Observability alert thresholds adjusted for streaming latency based on perf-canary results.
release_notes: OpenAI /v1/chat.completions parity improvements: role validation, stop sequence support during streaming, per-token logprobs exposure, improved streaming stability (chunk boundaries and backpressure), and structured output/function-call formatting. No breaking changes. See docs/openai-compat/chat_completions.md for migration notes and examples.
